Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

for preposition

on behalf of, in favour of

also on behalf of, in favour of, for me, for you, for one’s country

classical

Hor. C. 3.2.13: dulce et decōrum est prō patriā morī
Ter. Ph. 475: haud cessāvit prō tē ēnītī

prō + abl.

preposition with the ablative

for, on behalf of, in defence of

For the person or cause one works, speaks or fights for. The same word gives “instead of” and “in return for” (see instead; in exchange for).

Other words

  • cāsus datīvus — for (the person who gains by it)

    construction: the person in the dative, with no preposition · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.12: nec sibi sōlī, sed conjugī, līberīs

    The person something is done for, to his good or harm, stands in the dative.

  • nōmine + gen. — on behalf of, in the name of

    the ablative of nōmen, with a genitive or a possessive (meō, tuō nōmine) · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 1.16.16: Antōniō tuō nōmine grātiās ēgī

    When one acts as someone’s representative; see represent.

Examples

  • dulce et decōrum est prō patriā morī

    it is sweet and fitting to die for one’s countryHor. C. 3.2.13

  • Nisi Phaedria haud cessāvit prō tē ēnītī.

    Only, Phaedria hasn’t stopped working hard for you.Ter. Ph. 475

  • solet fierī. — rogāmus mittās. — posteā sī fēcerit, nēmō nostrum prō illō rogābit

    It happens. — Please let him off. — If he does it again, none of us will plead for him.Petr. 49.1

  • nec sibi sōlī, sed conjugī, līberīs cēterīsque, quōs cārōs habeat tuērīque dēbeat

    (nature makes a man provide) not for himself alone, but for his wife, his children and the others he holds dear and ought to protectCic. Off. 1.12

See also represent, instead, in exchange for, for.
